title: Painters in Gainesville, FL | Precision Paint Experts
description: Painters in Gainesville, FL for historic Duckpond homes, NW bungalows, and Haile Plantation builds. Licensed, insured, own crews. Free written estimates.
heroIntro: Our shop is a short drive west in Newberry, and Gainesville is where much of our week is spent: repainting houses and commercial buildings from the old streets of the Duckpond out to Haile Plantation and Town of Tioga. Precision Paint Experts is owned and run locally.

sections.h2: A painting contractor based one town over
body: Between the university, the hospitals, and the neighborhoods that grew up around them, Gainesville is one of the two biggest markets on our map. Our shop is in Newberry, just west of the city, so Gainesville jobs are on our regular route rather than a long drive away. That matters on day two of a project, when a crew lead needs to come back for a moisture reading, and it matters a year later if a door frame needs a touch-up under warranty.

Gainesville owners get a contractor that is licensed and bonded in Florida and fully insured, carrying workers' comp for each painter who sets foot on the job. The crew you meet on day one is on our payroll; no Gainesville contract gets passed along to a sub once you sign.

sections.h2: Gainesville's housing, from Duckpond to Town of Tioga
body: Few cities in the region mix building ages the way Gainesville does. The historic Duckpond and Pleasant Street districts contain the oldest houses on our schedule, and there the scope is driven by generations of stacked paint, old-growth wood that has swelled and shrunk for a century, and owners who want colors true to the era. Northwest Gainesville is full of postwar bungalows, which tend to need careful scraping and spot-priming at window sills, fascia, and the lowest courses of siding.

Haile Plantation and Town of Tioga sit at the opposite extreme, with newer houses whose repaints revolve around HOA color approvals, matching the existing trim, and upgrading tired builder paint. We also work regularly in Sweetwater Oaks, Mile Run, Westchester, Buckingham East, Kanapaha, and Golfview, so the estimate reflects what is actually typical on your street.

sections.h2: Why Gainesville paint fails: damp shade and hard sun
body: The failures we see across Gainesville are mostly moisture and sun failures. Under the live oaks, a muggy night leaves north walls wet well past sunrise, and that is all mildew and algae need. Sprinklers wet the same patch of stucco or siding every morning. Pollen season leaves a film that traps more moisture. Across the house, the sun-facing south and west sides are already chalky while the north side still looks fine.

So on Gainesville homes the default system is 100% acrylic on siding and trim, an elastomeric coating wherever stucco shows fine movement cracks, and a penetrating stain on bare decking or wood, drawn from premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore products. Our article on why humidity makes paint peel goes further into the moisture side.

sections.h2: How a Gainesville paint job runs, start to finish
body: You will meet a crew lead, not a sales rep, and that visit is normally booked within two days of your call. Expect a tape measure, photos of every elevation or room, and moisture readings on any stucco or wood that seems off. The written, itemized estimate generally reaches you the next business day, naming the surfaces we will and will not touch, the prep sequence, the specific primer and finish, the number of coats, and dates.

After approval, Gainesville jobs typically begin within one to three weeks. Our crews open with preparation: washing, mildew treatment, scraping and sanding, resetting popped nails, cutting out rotten fascia and trim, caulking, and spot-priming. Paint goes on next, two complete coats at minimum. Before we pack up, you walk the job with the crew lead and sign the punch list once everything on it is corrected. Exterior workmanship comes with written coverage of up to 10 years, and the leftover paint stays in your garage with labels on it.
Outside the city limits, the same crews handle the rest of Alachua County: Newberry, Alachua, Archer, Micanopy, Hawthorne, and High Springs.

faqs.q: Will you take on a historic house in the Duckpond or Pleasant Street district?
faqs.a: Yes. A century-old Gainesville house typically takes more scraping, sanding, and priming of bare wood than a newer build, and we break that prep out line by line on the estimate so the hours are visible.

faqs.q: When is the best season for an exterior repaint in Gainesville?
faqs.a: Fall through spring, roughly October to May, gives paint the easiest conditions in Gainesville. A summer exterior can still happen; the crew simply starts early and checks the dew point and radar through the day. Inside work has no season.

faqs.q: How quickly can you look at my Gainesville property?
faqs.a: A Gainesville walkthrough is typically set within 48 hours, and the written number follows one business day after the visit. Painting usually starts one to three weeks from approval.

faqs.q: Can my HOA or property manager get proof of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. Before a Gainesville community job starts, we send a certificate of insurance that names your association or management company as the holder.
